title: National Photonics Initiative backs House FY2021 funding for optics, photonics and quantum R&D
summary: NPI welcomed House appropriators' FY2021 increases for quantum and optics & photonics research, part of its push for National Quantum Initiative funding.

title: Nobel laureates protest a planned 30% cut to the Horizon Europe photonics partnership
summary: Open letter to the European Commission from Gérard Mourou, Stefan Hell and Theodor Hänsch warning that cutting photonics funding would be disastrous for Europe's technological goals.
change_note: Removed 'released by Photonics21': the source does not say so.

title: Photonics21 finalises 'New Horizons' 2021–27 research agenda and argues for a Horizon Europe partnership
summary: 'New Horizons – Securing Europe's technological sovereignty through Photonics', finalised at the end of November 2020 as the multi-annual roadmap for the photonics PPP, written as Horizon Europe moved away from technology-specific partnerships.

title: Export Control Law takes effect
summary: China's first comprehensive export-control statute, with dual-use lists and end-user rules; it is the legal basis for the later gallium, germanium and indium controls.

title: FY2021 NDAA authorises CHIPS for America semiconductor programmes
summary: Authorised the incentive and R&D programmes (including a national semiconductor technology centre and advanced packaging) that the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act later funded.
excluded_reason: The CHIPS for America sections of the FY2021 NDAA (15 U.S.C. 4651 ff.) do not name photonics, optics or lasers.

title: MIIT action plan for basic electronic components (2021–23) names optical-communication devices
summary: Sets a ¥2.1trn sales target for 2023 and lists optical-communication devices among key products for technology breakthroughs and stronger patent portfolios, alongside RF filters, high-speed connectors and MLCCs.

title: 14th Five-Year Plan and Vision 2035 adopted, with photonics among planned national laboratories
summary: Adopted by the National People's Congress in March 2021 from the Communist Party's October 2020 proposals. Calls for national laboratories in quantum information, photonics, micro- and nano-electronics and network communications, and lists integrated circuits and quantum information as frontier areas.

title: MIIT Dual-Gigabit Networks Action Plan (2021–2023)
summary: Set targets for gigabit fibre and 5G: fibre able to reach 200 million households and 20+ gigabit cities by end-2021, rising to 400 million households and 100 gigabit cities by end-2023, anchoring domestic demand for optical-communications equipment.
source: IT Home (full text of the MIIT plan)

title: Horizon Europe Photonics Partnership launched (Photonics21–Commission MoU)
amount_note: About €340M EC investment envisaged for 2021–27; €206M committed to 42 projects in 2021–24 (OPN, May 2024)
summary: The co-programmed partnership succeeded the Horizon 2020 photonics PPP and steers dedicated photonics calls under Horizon Europe, with Photonics21 drafting the research agenda.

title: AIM Photonics wins $321M seven-year renewal
amount_note: $165M federal (AFRL) + $156M non-federal cost share
summary: The Defense Department extended the Manufacturing USA institute for integrated photonics (Albany/Rochester, NY) for seven years, pairing AFRL funding with state, industry and university cost share to push defence-oriented silicon photonics.

title: Semicon India programme (₹76,000 crore) includes a compound-semiconductor and silicon-photonics fab scheme
technology: Silicon photonics; Compound semis / InP; Semiconductors (incl. photonics)
amount_note: ₹76,000 crore outlay
summary: Set up the India Semiconductor Mission; one scheme gives capital support (30%, raised to 50% in 2022) for compound-semiconductor, silicon-photonics and sensor fabs and packaging units.

title: C$90M to revitalise the NRC Canadian Photonics Fabrication Centre, plus C$150M Semiconductor Challenge Callout
technology: Compound semis / InP; Integrated photonics / PICs
amount_note: C$90M for CPFC (part of a C$240M package)
summary: Ottawa paired a C$150M Strategic Innovation Fund call for semiconductor projects with C$90M to upgrade the CPFC, North America's only publicly operated, open-access compound-semiconductor foundry.

title: National Growth Fund backs €1.1bn PhotonDelta integrated-photonics programme
amount_note: Up to €471.2M public from the National Growth Fund (often rounded to €470M), within €1.1bn incl. co-investment
summary: Six-year plan to scale the Dutch photonic-chip ecosystem: start-ups, InP and SiN foundries, design libraries and a target of 100,000+ wafers a year by 2030.

title: PERTE Chip: €12.25bn semiconductor plan names integrated photonics a strategic asset
amount_note: €12.25bn public to 2027; €150M for integrated-photonics R&D
summary: Spain's recovery-plan chip strategy earmarks €150M for integrated-photonics R&D within €1.165bn for scientific capacity, building on photonics groups at the Polytechnic Universities of Valencia and Madrid and the University of Vigo.

title: BMBF 'Quantum Systems' programme pools photonics and quantum technologies
summary: The research ministry put photonics and quantum technologies on an equal footing in one research programme, 'Quantensysteme – Spitzentechnologie entwickeln. Zukunft gestalten.'

title: EPIC convenes industry to draft a European PIC manufacturing strategy
summary: Workshops in Brussels (1 June) and Basel (20 September 2022) argued that research pilot lines alone will not give Europe volume PIC manufacturing, and set out what an industrial strategy would need.

title: CHIPS and Science Act signed into law
amount_note: $52.7B appropriated for semiconductor programmes
summary: Created the incentive, R&D and DoD Microelectronics Commons programmes that later funded photonic-chip fabs (Infinera, Coherent) and lithography-optics suppliers (Corning).

title: BIS export controls on advanced computing and chipmaking equipment
summary: The 7 October rules restricted exports of advanced chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment to China and set off the US–Dutch–Japanese alignment on lithography controls; they were widened again in 2023 and 2024.

title: Photonics Germany alliance asks for photonics to stay central in the Quantum Systems programme
summary: Position paper welcoming equal standing for photonics and quantum in the new programme and asking for photonics funding to target the coalition agreement's future fields; cites 170,000+ jobs and €47bn+ sector revenue in 2021.

title: National Quantum Strategy launched with C$360M
amount_note: C$360M (Budget 2021 commitment)
summary: Sets missions for quantum computing, quantum-secure communications and quantum sensing. The strategy text names quantum photonics among its sensing calls and lasers among Canada's quantum-derived innovations.
source: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (strategy text)

title: National Quantum Mission approved (₹6,003.65 crore, 2023–31)
summary: Four thematic hubs (computing, communication, sensing & metrology, materials & devices); goals include single-photon and entangled-photon sources and satellite-based secure quantum communication between ground stations 2,000 km apart.
change_note: Quantum-communication goal reworded to match the Cabinet release (satellite links between ground stations 2,000 km apart).

title: Photonics21 hands Commission new research agenda: “A Path towards Strategic Autonomy”
summary: Strategic Research and Innovation Agenda setting photonics priorities across European value chains for the Horizon Europe Photonics Partnership's next five years.

title: National Quantum Strategy published
summary: Federal plan to build Australia's quantum industry; its technology map lists photonics and optics among enabling capabilities. It underpins later measures such as the Critical Technologies Challenge Program.
source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources

title: National Semiconductor Strategy: up to £1bn over ten years
amount_note: Up to £1bn over 10 years; £200M for 2023–25
summary: Twenty-year plan focused on design/IP, R&D and compound semiconductors; the compound-semiconductor goal is meant to complement and interface with the UK's photonics expertise.

title: Revised Semiconductor and Digital Industry Strategy makes photonics-electronics convergence a key goal
summary: METI targets ¥15trn domestic chip sales by 2030 and commits to R&D and deployment of next-generation chips and photonics-electronics convergence; a Green Innovation Fund project aims to cut data-centre energy by over 40% with optical wiring.

title: IPCEI on Microelectronics and Communication Technologies approved, with photonics firms taking part
amount_note: Up to €8.1bn state aid from 14 member states; €13.7bn private expected
summary: 68 projects from 56 companies; participants include TRUMPF, Carl Zeiss, OSRAM Opto Semiconductors, Vigo Photonics, ADVA and Teledyne.

title: Export licensing imposed on gallium and germanium items
summary: From 1 August 2023, 14 gallium- and germanium-related items (incl. GaAs, GaN, Ge ingots) need MOFCOM licences – inputs for lasers, photodetectors, IR optics and fibre.

title: Export controls on 23 types of chipmaking equipment, incl. lithography
summary: METI added cleaning, deposition, annealing, lithography, etching and testing tools to its control list after talks with the US and Netherlands.

title: Licence requirement for advanced DUV immersion lithography takes effect
summary: ASML must seek Dutch licences to ship its most advanced immersion DUV systems; the list was later extended to further NXT models, aligning with US rules.

title: DoD Microelectronics Commons: eight hubs selected ($238M first awards)
amount_note: $238M initial awards of a $2B FY23–27 programme
summary: CHIPS-funded lab-to-fab prototyping network of eight regional hubs in seven states; focus areas include quantum technology and 5G/6G.

title: European Chips Act enters into force (Regulation 2023/1781)
amount_note: More than €43bn of policy-driven public and private investment
summary: Created the Chips for Europe Initiative and Chips JU pilot lines – the route that later funded the PIXEurope photonic-chip pilot line.

title: Photonics named among EU critical technologies for economic security
summary: Commission Recommendation listing 10 critical technology areas; ‘advanced semiconductors’ – explicitly including photonics – is one of four flagged for immediate risk assessment with member states.

title: CSIS 'Controlling Light' flags silicon photonics as an emerging front in US–China tech competition
summary: Analysis by Matthew Reynolds arguing that silicon photonics may become strategically important as transistor scaling slows, and examining China's push into the field and the US policy response.

title: National Technology Strategy puts optics & integrated photonics first of ten priorities
summary: Cabinet-approved strategy aiming for world leadership in integrated-photonics design and manufacturing by 2035; action agendas for each technology followed in January 2026.

title: METI/NEDO grant of ~¥45bn for NTT-led photonics-electronics convergence
technology: Integrated photonics / PICs; Optical comms & interconnects
amount_note: ¥45.2bn over five years (post-5G fund)
summary: Supports optical chiplets, photonic-interface memory modules and IOWN-related computing, replacing electrical links between chips with optical ones from FY2028 onward.

title: Pentagon lists LiDAR maker Hesai as a Chinese military company (1260H)
summary: The Defense Department added the automotive-LiDAR maker to its Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies on 31 Jan 2024; a federal court later ruled against Hesai's challenge. The FY2024 NDAA bars DoD from contracting with listed firms from mid-2026, and the listing underpins later bills targeting Chinese LiDAR.
source: House Select Committee on the CCP

title: S$180M National Semiconductor Translation & Innovation Centre for flat optics and silicon photonics
summary: A*STAR centre at Fusionopolis (opening April 2024) giving firms shared lines to prototype flat-optics and silicon-photonics devices.
change_note: Date corrected to the announcement (Fri 1 Mar 2024); 8 Mar was the EDB write-up.

title: A$940M federal–Queensland package for PsiQuantum's photonic quantum computer
amount_note: Almost A$1bn: about A$470M in equity and loans from each of the Commonwealth and Queensland
summary: The Commonwealth and Queensland each commit about A$470M in equity and loans for PsiQuantum to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer, based on photonic qubits, in Brisbane.
source: Prime Minister of Australia (joint release with Queensland)
change_note: Wording now follows the joint release (fault-tolerant computer in Brisbane).

title: Critical Raw Materials Act in force – gallium and germanium are strategic materials
summary: Sets extraction, processing and recycling benchmarks and fast-tracks strategic projects for 17 strategic raw materials, including gallium and germanium used in photonic devices.

title: UKTIN expert group calls for an open-access integrated-photonics pilot capability
technology: Integrated photonics / PICs; Optical comms & interconnects
summary: A Future Capability Paper by the Optical Communications and Photonics expert working group of the UK Telecom Innovation Network, written for the Future Telecoms strategy, recommends open-access pilot capabilities for integrated photonic chips (fabrication, assembly and packaging) at prototype-to-pilot scale, a long-term all-optical networks programme modelled on Japan's IOWN, and a fibre-rich national test network.

title: SEMI launches Silicon Photonics Industry Alliance (SiPhIA) with TSMC and ASE
summary: Formed by 30+ companies at SEMICON Taiwan; now 110+ members working on a 2024–27 technology blueprint and standards for co-packaged optics. Three special interest groups launched on 11 April 2025.

title: Queensland awards A$53M in quantum and advanced-technology grants, incl. photonics facilities
amount_note: A$53M across five state programmes (strategy and Quantum Academy: A$89.7M over five years)
photonics_amount_note: A$10.3M: A$6.3M National Advanced Photonics Facility (UQ) and A$4M CSIRO photonic-chip packaging
summary: State-level awards under the Queensland Quantum and Advanced Technologies Strategy. They include A$6.3M for the University of Queensland's National Advanced Photonics Facility and A$4M for CSIRO to package integrated photonic chips.
change_note: Strategy figure corrected to A$89.7M (it was A$83.7M).

title: CHIPS NAPMP opens up to $1.6bn advanced-packaging R&D competition, incl. photonic connectors
amount_note: Up to ~$1.6bn across five R&D areas
summary: One of the five R&D areas is connector technology, including photonics and RF; concept papers were due 20 December 2024.

title: House China Committee urges controls on silicon photonics
summary: Chair Moolenaar and Ranking Member Krishnamoorthi asked Commerce to investigate PRC photonics firms and add silicon-photonics equipment and products to the Commerce Control List.
source: House Select Committee on the CCP

title: Chips JU selects PIXEurope for €380M photonic-integrated-circuit pilot line
technology: Integrated photonics / PICs; Silicon photonics; Compound semis / InP
amount_note: €380M total; EU share up to €190M (call Chips-2024-CPL-5, 24 Jul – 16 Sep 2024), rest from participating states
summary: Fifth Chips Act pilot line: an open-access PIC value chain (design to packaging) across ~20 institutes in 11 countries, coordinated by ICFO and running to 2030.

title: Netherlands commits €66.3M to PIXEurope sites in Eindhoven and Enschede
amount_note: €66.3M national (€53.8M brought forward from PhotonDelta's growth-fund money + €12.5M from the Economic Affairs ministry), matched by €66.3M EU = €132.6M
summary: Dutch share of the pilot line, to be matched by EU funding once negotiations conclude.

title: Ban in principle on gallium, germanium and antimony exports to the US
summary: MOFCOM Announcement No. 46 barred licences for US-bound Ga, Ge, Sb and superhard materials and banned dual-use exports to US military users; the US-specific clause was suspended in Nov 2025.

title: CHIPS preliminary terms: up to $33M for Coherent's first 150 mm InP line
technology: Compound semis / InP; Optical comms & interconnects
amount_note: Up to $33M (non-binding preliminary memorandum of terms)
summary: To modernise a cleanroom at the Sherman, Texas site for InP optoelectronic devices (about 70 jobs). No final award was published; Commerce signed a separate letter of intent for up to $50M in June 2026, and NIST's project page now shows that figure.
change_note: Re-sourced: NIST's project page was edited in June 2026 and now shows the later $50M figure. Date set to the 5 Dec 2024 announcement.

title: CHIPS award of up to $32M to Corning for lithography-grade optical glass
amount_note: Up to $32M direct funding
summary: Expands US output of HPFS fused silica and ULE glass used in DUV/EUV lithography optics and photomasks, in Canton, NY.

title: CHIPS award of up to $93M to Infinera for InP photonic-chip fab and packaging
technology: Compound semis / InP; Optical comms & interconnects
amount_note: Up to $93M direct funding
summary: Finalised award to expand indium-phosphide PIC fabrication (San Jose, CA) and advanced test & packaging (Bethlehem, PA), about a tenfold capacity increase.

title: Export controls extended to indium (incl. indium phosphide) and four other metals
summary: Decision No. 10 of 2025 requires licences for tungsten, tellurium, bismuth, molybdenum and indium items – including InP and trimethylindium used for lasers and datacom chips.

title: Cambridge and Southampton join PIXEurope with up to £4.2M from DSIT
amount_note: Up to £4.2M, match-funded by Horizon Europe
summary: UK participation in the EU Chips JU's photonics pilot line, a year after the UK joined the Chips JU, via Southampton's Cornerstone Photonics Innovation Centre and the Cambridge Graphene Centre.
change_note: Removed 'first UK participation': the source does not say so.

title: National Development Council makes silicon photonics a priority “economic shield”
summary: NDC Minister Paul Liu said Taiwan will prioritise silicon photonics, building on its packaging and foundry strengths, as tariff pressures mount.

title: SPIE mobilises photonics community to defend US federal S&T funding
summary: Advocacy campaign and sign-on letters urging Congress to sustain funding for science and for optics and photonics as agency budgets came under pressure.

title: Photonics Leadership Group: “UK Photonics 2025 – The Hidden Economic Engine”
summary: Sizes UK photonics at £18.5bn output (2024) and 84,800 jobs and sets out five actions, including backing UK photonics components in challenge-focused programmes.

title: €17.2M state stake in SPARC III-V photonic-chip foundry (PERTE Chip)
technology: Compound semis / InP; Integrated photonics / PICs
amount_note: €17.2M equity via SETT
summary: Supports Spain's first InP/GaAs PIC manufacturing plant in Vigo, framed as a dual-use, strategic-autonomy asset.

title: Industrial Strategy sector plan makes semiconductors, incl. photonics, a frontier technology
technology: Semiconductors (incl. photonics); Compound semis / InP; Photonics (broad)
summary: The Digital and Technologies Sector Plan names six frontier technologies; for semiconductors it builds on UK strengths in chip design, compound semiconductors and photonics, and funds a UK Semiconductor Centre (up to £19M).

title: FABrIC (C$223M, five years) funds first semiconductor & photonics challenge projects
amount_note: C$223M programme; first round C$35.6M incl. C$13.4M ISED
summary: First round of the CMC Microsystems-run initiative: 20 projects across photonics, MEMS, quantum and compound semiconductors. A May 2026 challenge added C$10.7M for 11 projects in edge AI, optical interconnects and sensing.

title: Quantum Europe Strategy sets path to a 2026 Quantum Act
summary: Aims for EU quantum leadership by 2030 with a quantum design facility and six quantum-chip pilot lines under the Chips JU; promised a Quantum Act in 2026, with a call for evidence opened at the end of October 2025.

title: Cabinet releases a further €100.8M for PhotonDelta, leaving €50M conditional
amount_note: €100.8M converted, so €421.2M of the €471.2M in the 2022 award is now definitive; €50M stays conditional (part of the 2022 amount, so not charted again)
summary: Follows a June 2025 opinion from the growth-fund advisory committee. On 17 July 2026 the RVO agency granted up to €64.1M for Phase 2 (2026–28). The growth-fund plan also backs PhotonDelta's €60M Startup Fund (launched 2024), which lends €250k–€2M per start-up.

title: Ten Major AI Infrastructure Projects make silicon photonics a core technology
summary: Premier Cho's programme names silicon photonics, quantum technology and AI robotics as its three core technologies; in 2026 the Economic Affairs ministry opened a silicon-photonics R&D initiative under its A+ programme, aiming for a self-reliant CPO supply chain.
change_note: Date corrected to Premier Cho's post (Tue 22 Jul 2025).

title: CAS Academic Divisions report urges a national research plan on photonics-electronics convergence
technology: Integrated photonics / PICs; Silicon photonics; Optical comms & interconnects
summary: A strategic research report published by the Chinese Academy of Sciences Academic Divisions finds China's process platforms scattered and short of design software, packaging standards and volume manufacturing. It recommends that the National Natural Science Foundation launch a major research plan on photonics-electronics convergence and integration, more central R&D funding, common design standards and a public process platform for optoelectronic chips.
source: Chinese Academy of Sciences Academic Divisions

title: Hightech Agenda Deutschland adopted (six key technologies)
technology: Quantum photonics; Lasers, LiDAR & sensing; Semiconductors (incl. photonics)
summary: Prioritises AI, quantum technologies, microelectronics, biotechnology, fusion and climate-neutral energy, and climate-neutral mobility. Photonics is not a key technology in its own right; optics appears in a field-ready optical atomic clock goal and in laser-fusion plans. First roadmaps came in May 2026.

title: €62.1M awarded for Spain's integrated-photonics pilot line
amount_note: €62.1M (PERTE Chip)
summary: Funds Spanish nodes covering design, fabrication, packaging and testing, tied to the European PIC pilot line.

title: FDD Action urges procurement bans and 1260H listings for Chinese LiDAR
summary: Policy alert arguing Chinese firms hold ~80% of LiDAR sales and calling on Congress to bar them from defence, transport and infrastructure projects.

title: SPIE and 50+ societies ask Congress to revisit grant-oversight executive order
summary: Coalition letter on the 7 August 2025 EO ‘Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking’, seeking protection for merit-based peer review.
excluded_reason: The coalition letter concerns federal grant oversight in general and does not name photonics.

title: Bosch, VW, Nokia and others back call for a €2bn stand-alone FP10 photonics programme
amount_note: Requested: €2bn EU programme to unlock €6–8bn co-investment
summary: End-user statement from Bosch, Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, Nokia Bell Labs, TRUMPF, ZEISS, SCHOTT and others asking for a €2bn stand-alone photonics programme in FP10, Grand Challenges and stronger supply chains for critical components.

title: CORNERSTONE policy workshop calls for a national silicon-photonics pilot line and delivery plan
summary: Outputs of a London workshop on 15 Oct 2025 convened by the CORNERSTONE Photonics Innovation Centre (University of Southampton, with Glasgow and STFC). Asks government for a long-term national silicon-photonics delivery plan led by one department, a business case for a shared pre-competitive pilot line co-funded by government capital, Innovate UK and the UK Infrastructure Bank, a national cluster audit, and a coordination function, possibly under the UK Semiconductor Centre.

title: US-specific gallium/germanium/antimony ban suspended to 27 Nov 2026
summary: MOFCOM Announcement No. 72 of 2025 paused the US-specific clause of the Dec 2024 ban after the Trump–Xi meeting; licensing for these metals and the ban on US military end-users stayed in force. On 9 Nov 2026 China extended a separate pause on its October-2025 controls to 10 Jan 2027 but published no extension of this one.
watch_note: Pause on China's ban on US-bound gallium, germanium and antimony exports ends unless extended; no extension published as of 20 Nov 2026

title: CFR Task Force flags single-supplier risk in lasers and optics, urges duty waivers for allied photonics parts
summary: Independent Task Force report on US economic security lists laser diodes, mirrors and amplifiers among single-supplier risks for quantum equipment and proposes waiving import duties on quantum-enabling lasers, optics and photonics components from allies; onshoring calls cover chemicals, PCBs and IC substrates.

title: A*STAR and GlobalFoundries plan a silicon-photonics R&D centre after GF buys AMF
summary: GlobalFoundries acquired Advanced Micro Foundry, the A*STAR spin-off silicon-photonics foundry. A*STAR and GF will sign a master research collaboration agreement and set up a centre of excellence on next-generation materials for 400 Gbps-class links.

title: SPECTARIS asks Berlin to strengthen quantum and photonics technologies
summary: Policy recommendations from the German optics and photonics industry association: consolidate quantum and photonics funding into long-term national and EU instruments, prioritise market-ready quantum sensing and communication, build testbeds, pilot lines and European photonics manufacturing to secure supply chains, and expand training and skilled immigration.

title: SAFE LiDAR Act introduced to phase out Chinese-made LiDAR
summary: Would restrict new federal and critical-infrastructure use of LiDAR from foreign-adversary-linked firms at once (legacy kit gets five years) and bar new transactions nationwide after three years, with waivers and research carve-outs. Select Committee Chair Moolenaar co-sponsored in June 2026; still in committee.
source: House Select Committee on the CCP (Democrats)
watch_note: SAFE LiDAR Act lapses unless enacted before the 119th Congress ends

title: FY2026 NDAA adds gallium, germanium and molybdenum to DoD restricted materials
summary: Extends 10 U.S.C. 4872 sourcing restrictions on covered nations (China, Russia, Iran, North Korea) to these materials; the Ga/Ge restriction starts 18 Dec 2027.
watch_note: DoD ban on gallium and germanium from covered nations takes effect

title: Photonics Leadership Group compiles industry requests to Government
summary: Community input from a 29 January 2026 meeting: a national roadmap, capital-expenditure support, skills capacity and better coordination between clusters.

title: MSIT launches next-generation optical computing semiconductor programme
technology: Integrated photonics / PICs; Optical comms & interconnects
amount_note: ₩235.1bn 2026 core-technology plan (chips, displays, batteries)
summary: MSIT's 2026 core source-technology plan (₩235.1bn across chips, displays and batteries) starts a new project on next-generation optical-computing semiconductors.
source: MSIT press release (via Univ. of Seoul)

title: Section 232 critical-minerals proclamation names gallium and germanium in fibre-optic networks; negotiations first
summary: Proclamation 11001 found that imports of processed critical minerals threaten US national security, noting that the communications sector uses gallium, germanium and indium in fibre-optic networks; it chose negotiations with a 180-day window rather than immediate tariffs. A separate proclamation the same day put a 25% tariff on a narrow set of advanced chips.

title: Chips JU launches P4Q photonics-for-quantum pilot line
amount_note: €50M public (€25M Chips JU + €25M national); total cost €51.5M
summary: 29 partners in 12 countries, coordinated by the University of Twente, building pilot-scale integrated-photonics processes for quantum devices; runs April 2026 to March 2029.

title: Photonic-chip CEOs urge priority in the Chips Act revision
summary: CEO steering committee (Aixtron, Almae, Ligentec, PHIX, SMART Photonics, Soitec, VLC Photonics, X-FAB) with PhotonDelta asks for a dedicated photonic-chip programme in Chips Act 2.0, investment in open-access foundries, simpler rules and easier scale-up finance.

title: Critical Technologies Challenge Program: A$12.7M to eight quantum demonstrators
amount_note: A$12.7M, Round 1 Stage 2 (programme up to A$36M)
summary: Stage 2 demonstrators include quantum optical imaging for diabetes assessment (Miniprobes) and quantum antennas for through-earth communications in mining (Orica).

title: India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 announced in Union Budget 2026–27
summary: Moves the mission from ecosystem start-up to deepening; budget lines include a modified scheme for compound semiconductors, silicon photonics, sensors and ATMP/OSAT units. The Cabinet approved ISM 2.0 with a ₹1.275 trn outlay on 15 July 2026.

title: EPIC position paper calls for a whole-sector European photonics competitiveness strategy
amount_note: Asks for at least €2bn for photonics in the 2028–34 EU budget
summary: Argues that PICs are only part of the photonics economy and that Europe needs a strategy and dedicated funding covering the whole sector, not just chips.

title: Council for Science and Technology advises PM to make photonics a national priority
summary: Letter to the Prime Minister dated 19 February 2026, published 9 March, urging that photonics be treated as a national priority: publish a photonics roadmap (asked for by April 2026), use public procurement as an early market, and widen international partnerships and exports. The Institute of Physics welcomed it the same day.
source: GOV.UK (CST letter to the Prime Minister)

title: 15th Five-Year Plan approved – optoelectronic chips among semiconductor priorities
summary: Approved by the National People's Congress on 12 March 2026; calls for 'extraordinary measures' for S&T self-reliance and lists mature-node, advanced and optoelectronic chips among semiconductor priorities.

title: NEDO backs LSTC photonics-electronics packaging R&D hub in Chitose
technology: Integrated photonics / PICs; Optical comms & interconnects
summary: LSTC was selected to develop packaging technology that accelerates photonics-electronics convergence and to build an open R&D hub for 300 mm panel back-end processing at the Chitose Institute of Science and Technology, next to Rapidus, due for completion in FY2028; imec is a technical partner.

title: Work starts on a UK National Photonics Roadmap after CST advice
summary: The Photonics Leadership Group and government partners invited the community to help draft the roadmap asked for by the CST: an online consultation, then an in-person workshop in May 2026. No roadmap had been published by mid-November 2026.

title: MeitY launches indigenous silicon-photonics PDK and PIC test engine
summary: Shared national tools from the IIT Madras centre of excellence; officials floated a silicon-photonics fab with packaging under ISM 2.0.

title: National Quantum Initiative Reauthorization clears Senate and House committees
summary: S.3597 (Senate Commerce, 14 Apr) and H.R.8462 (House Science, 29 Apr) would extend the NQI to December 2034 with a stronger manufacturing and applications focus; floor votes pending.
watch_note: National Quantum Initiative reauthorisation lapses unless enacted before the 119th Congress ends

title: Canada to spin off the Canadian Photonics Fabrication Centre as a commercial entity
technology: Compound semis / InP; Integrated photonics / PICs
summary: The NRC will begin spinning off the CPFC into a commercial entity 'with firmly Canadian foundations', following Budget 2025's commitment to look at drawing in private capital to scale the foundry for AI-era photonic chips.

title: CORNERSTONE makes the case for a £305M UK silicon-photonics pilot line
summary: Publishes a survey of 100 UK decision-makers (fieldwork March 2026) with a business case for a national open-access pilot line combining wafer fabrication, heterogeneous integration and packaging. The case asks for about £305M of capital as a grant (roughly £185M for equipment and £120M for the building) and estimates £2.9bn of added value and about 2,850 jobs by 2040; 74% of respondents said a pilot line would speed innovation.

title: CHIPS quantum letters of intent: $2.013bn to nine firms, incl. up to $100M for PsiQuantum's photonic platform
amount_note: $2.013bn across nine LOIs; PsiQuantum up to $100M; GlobalFoundries $375M
summary: Nine letters of intent for two quantum foundries and seven quantum-computing firms. PsiQuantum's covers electro-optic materials, high-temperature single-photon detectors and ultra-low-loss photonic packaging; GlobalFoundries' foundry spans photonic and other modalities. Both were finalised on 8 September 2026.

title: Photonics France presses the President for a national photonics plan
summary: At the event where President Macron announced €1bn more for the national quantum strategy and France's part in a €550M semiconductor IPCEI, the national photonics federation repeated its call for a national photonics plan and for securing a photonics public-private partnership with its own budget.

title: +€1bn for the national quantum strategy and €550M for the IPCEI on advanced semiconductor technologies
amount_note: €1bn (France 2030) for quantum + €550M French contribution to IPCEI-AST
summary: Announced by President Macron at the CEA's TGCC on 22 May 2026, adding to the €1.8bn 2021–25 quantum plan; France will also put €550M into the IPCEI on Advanced Semiconductor Technologies.
change_note: €550M described as France's IPCEI contribution, as the source puts it.

title: techUK report: publish a roadmap and empower the UK Semiconductor Centre
summary: Eight recommendations, from a National Photonics Roadmap and better cluster mapping to skills outreach, warning of a narrowing window for UK leadership.

title: PHOTONICS GERMANY asks for a €2bn FP10 photonics programme and faster export licences
summary: Joint paper by SPECTARIS and OptecNet Deutschland after the PHOTONICS GERMANY Future Summit. Asks the federal government to push for a stand-alone FP10 photonics programme of at least €2bn for 2028–34, anchor photonics in the Hightech Agenda roadmaps, fund industrial collective research (IGF) with at least €300M a year, build production-near pilot lines, and make export-licence reviews between the economy ministry and the Foreign Office faster and more transparent.

title: Commission proposes Chips Act 2.0, adding photonics and PICs
summary: Would replace Regulation 2023/1781, explicitly add photonics and PICs to a reinforced Chips for Europe Initiative 2.0, speed up pilot-line industrialisation and add demand-side measures. ITRE leads in Parliament (rapporteur Oliver Schenk, appointed 31 Aug 2026). The Commission says more than €52bn has been committed to production facilities under the first Act. The Council aims to agree its position by December 2026.
watch_note: No date set: Council position targeted for December 2026; Parliament (ITRE) report pending
change_note: Removed an unsupported jobs figure; added the Council's timetable.

title: Pentagon adds optical-transceiver maker Innolight and LiDAR maker RoboSense to its 1260H list
technology: Optical comms & interconnects; Lasers, LiDAR & sensing
summary: The Defense Department's June 2026 update to its Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies added Zhongji Innolight, a leading supplier of data-centre optical transceivers, and LiDAR maker RoboSense; Hesai stayed listed. From 30 June 2026 the FY2024 NDAA bars DoD from contracting directly with listed firms.
change_note: Added on 20 Nov 2026; earlier updates had missed it.

title: Photonics21 hands the Commission its 2028–34 research agenda for FP10
amount_note: Asks for a €2bn stand-alone FP10 photonics programme
summary: The Photonics SRIA 2028–2034 warns that over half of EU photonics firms depend on Chinese suppliers and asks for a €2bn stand-alone FP10 programme, photonics as a pillar of Chips JU 2.0 and eight Grand Challenges in areas such as AI, defence and space.

title: CHIPS letter of intent: up to $50M for Coherent's 6-inch InP fab in Texas
technology: Compound semis / InP; Optical comms & interconnects
amount_note: Up to $50M (letter of intent, not final)
summary: Would expand the Sherman, TX site – described as the first and largest high-volume 150 mm indium-phosphide fab – for AI data-centre optical links.

title: CORNERSTONE white paper: manufacturing access is the main barrier to commercialising silicon photonics
summary: 'Silicon Photonics: The window of opportunity is open' reports a survey of 500 decision-makers in the UK, US, Netherlands, Germany and Spain: 66% name manufacturing access as the main roadblock to commercialisation, 59% say their country lacks the infrastructure to move from research to market, and 32% cite tariffs as the biggest prototyping barrier. It asks the UK government for a national pilot line (a National PIC Foundry, about £305M of capital) and a dedicated photonics strategy.

title: Industry and lawmakers propose national CPO programme and Gwangju optical-chip hub
technology: Optical comms & interconnects; Integrated photonics / PICs
summary: At a Gwangju policy meeting hosted by Rep. Ahn Do-geol, the Korea Optical Convergence Industry Promotion Association proposed AI-chip optical-interconnect and CPO R&D as a new national programme with shared test and evaluation infrastructure; participants also asked for a dedicated industry body.

title: PhotonDelta and BOM urge Defence to adopt Dutch photonic chips
summary: A study by PhotonDelta and the Brabant Development Agency, handed to State Secretary for Defence Derk Boswijk, argues that integrated photonic chips strengthen navigation and timing without GPS, secure communication, sensing and resilience to electronic warfare. It calls for programmatic and closer collaboration between Defence, industry and knowledge institutions to speed adoption.

title: Executive Order 14415 tightens defence sourcing waivers for critical materials
summary: Directs the Department of War to curb waivers, map supply chains to the mine and require alternative sourcing; most non-availability waivers stop from 1 Jan 2027.
watch_note: Most DoD non-availability waivers for China-sourced covered materials stop
change_note: Waiver change described as the order does: most non-availability waivers stop; national-security waivers remain.

title: Photonics21 welcomes Chips Act 2.0 and seeks ring-fenced photonics funding
summary: Calls the explicit inclusion of photonics and integrated photonics an important strategic recognition, but asks for a separate ring-fenced budget for the wider photonics ecosystem via an MoU-based partnership under Horizon Europe and the European Competitiveness Fund.

title: Senate Commerce passes Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (S.4429)
summary: Would ban foreign-adversary connected-vehicle technology and vehicles, phasing restrictions in from 2027; Chinese LiDAR suppliers such as Hesai feature in the debate. Approved by voice vote; awaits a Senate floor vote (House companion H.R.8730).
excluded_reason: The bill text of S.4429 (introduced 29 Apr 2026) does not mention LiDAR, lasers or optics.

title: CHIPS letters of intent: $874M to seven firms, incl. up to $300M for GlobalFoundries co-packaged optics
technology: Optical comms & interconnects; Silicon photonics; Semiconductors (incl. photonics)
amount_note: $874M across seven letters of intent (GlobalFoundries up to $300M; Aeluma $30M); not final
photonics_amount_note: Up to $300M for GlobalFoundries' co-packaged optics (letter of intent)
summary: Preliminary awards for compute supply-chain R&D; final amounts depend on further due diligence and approval by Commerce.

title: Reported plan for an FCC ban on new Chinese optical transceiver models
summary: Reuters reported on 4 Aug 2026 that the administration is drafting an FCC ban on new models of Chinese optical transceivers and other data-centre devices, and on 17 Nov that it is pressing ahead despite lobbying by Amazon, Google, Meta and others. Chinese vendors hold about two-thirds of the market. Nothing has been published; the FCC could still change or drop it.
watch_note: No date set; watch for an FCC notice

title: National Security S&T Strategy adds integrated photonics to critical-technology list
summary: OSTP's strategy rewrites the critical-technology list: integrated photonics is added under semiconductors, optical links and fibre sit under communications, and photonic computing is a future technology of note; data centres were dropped.

title: Strategic Response Fund backs Xanadu's photonic quantum-computer manufacturing
amount_note: C$195M federal contribution toward a C$893M project
summary: Federal support for Xanadu to scale up advanced quantum manufacturing in Canada.
source: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
change_note: Dropped 'repayable': the release does not say so.

title: Semicon 2.0 notified (₹1.275 trn); photonics fabs eligible for 35% capex support
technology: Integrated photonics / PICs; Compound semis / InP; Semiconductors (incl. photonics)
amount_note: ₹1.275 trillion
summary: Cabinet-approved on 15 July and notified on 31 August 2026 as a single six-pillar scheme; Category 6 covers compound-semiconductor, photonics, sensor/MEMS and discrete fabs (photonics fabs from 100 mm wafers) with 35% of eligible capex.

title: MIIT/NDRC five-year plan for electronic-information manufacturing
summary: Issued by MIIT and NDRC on 15 Sep 2026: targets more than ¥30trn revenue for larger firms by 2030 and makes strengthening the photonics industry one of five foundation tasks, with shared photonic-electronic integration process platforms and more supply of integrated optical chips, transceiver modules and LiDAR.
change_note: Re-sourced to the official Q&A; summary now quotes the plan's photonics task.

title: Quantum industry consortium asks Chips Act 2.0 to cover visible and UV photonics
summary: QuIC's response to the Chips Act 2.0 proposal asks that the Act's photonics objectives cover visible, deep-blue and ultraviolet integration, which trapped-ion and neutral-atom machines need, not only telecom and datacom platforms. It also asks for a multi-project wafer programme, cryogenic test and packaging facilities, and a route for quantum chip manufacturing into the Act's priority areas.

title: SG Semiconductor launched; S$800M RIE flagship includes silicon photonics
amount_note: S$800M RIE Flagship in Semiconductors, 2026–30
summary: Silicon photonics and flat optics are two of seven focus areas; A*STAR and GlobalFoundries will deepen 300 mm silicon-photonics R&D and A*STAR works on co-packaged optics.

title: Critical Technologies Challenge Program: A$12.3M to six more quantum projects
amount_note: A$12.3M, Round 2 Stage 2
summary: Six company-led consortia, including Silicon Quantum Computing (A$3.6M) and QuantX Labs (A$2.2M) for a quantum clock that keeps the electricity grid timed without external signals.
source: Department of Industry, Science and Resources
excluded_reason: The Round 2 Stage 2 announcement names quantum computing, clocks and biosensors but not photonics or optics.

title: MIC opens All-Photonics Network Innovation Hub
summary: National testbed built by Mitsubishi Research Institute under a Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications commission, with core sites in Otemachi, Shinjuku and Yokosuka. Firms and universities can test uses such as low-latency remote robotics and AI on remote GPUs. Bookings opened 1 October; it opened 5 October 2026.

title: Wilson Center urges a US photonics strategy and non-Chinese indium phosphide supply
technology: Optical comms & interconnects; Compound semis / InP; Integrated photonics / PICs
summary: Commentary by a Wilson Center research fellow on US–China competition in optical interconnects. Recommends that Washington publish a photonics strategy naming the supply-chain layers it intends to own (foundry capacity, packaging, lasers), fund pilot lines for data-centre photonics, use public money for indium phosphide substrate and high-speed laser capacity outside China, and coordinate standards and testing with Taiwan, Japan and Europe.

title: NEDO selects consortium for mass-production of photonics-electronics devices
technology: Integrated photonics / PICs; Silicon photonics; Compound semis / InP
amount_note: Amount not disclosed
summary: NTT Innovative Devices with Japan Semiconductor, Furukawa Electric and Shinko aim for a >10x productivity gain and a pilot production line for optical chiplets.

title: China extends pause on Oct-2025 export controls to 10 Jan 2027
summary: MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 58 of 2026 keeps six October-2025 measures (rare-earth, battery-material, graphite-anode and superhard-material controls) suspended from 11 November 2026 to 10 January 2027; the separate US-specific Ga/Ge/Sb pause still ends on 27 November.
watch_note: US–China truce and China's suspended export controls run out
excluded_reason: The six October-2025 measures it pauses cover rare earths, battery materials, graphite and superhard materials, not gallium, germanium or optics.

title: Draft EU Quantum Act would favour European suppliers
summary: A draft seen by The Quantum Insider would largely limit strategic quantum projects and public procurement to EU-controlled firms, require quantum-safe procurement in critical sectors, keep a list of critical quantum components and monitor supply dependencies; an official told MLex in September the proposal could slip into 2027.
watch_note: Commission proposal expected; may slip into 2027

title: PhotonDelta Phase II funds national photonic quantum computing mission
amount_note: Amount not disclosed
summary: Under Phase II of the PhotonDelta growth-fund programme, QuiX Quantum and Dutch partners run a January 2026 – December 2028 mission developing the components and a manufacturing strategy for a 100+ qubit universal photonic quantum computer.
source: QuiX Quantum press release (via The Quantum Insider)
change_note: Partner count dropped: the source gives both seven and nine.

title: imec opens photonics R&D presence in Hokkaido with METI backing
summary: imec's first R&D base in Japan, at Hokkaido University's Sapporo campus, focused on photonics and co-packaged optics; backed by METI and working with LSTC.
